title: Match object revisions before bounding range reads
applies_when: A versioned object reader accepts a generation or revision separately from the path, obtains size through info(), then bounds sequential or concurrent reads or cache fills with that metadata. Exercise each size-lookup caller, not just the metadata API.
lesson: Trace the version selector through metadata lookup as well as the data request. A correct generation on the download URL cannot compensate for a size obtained from the latest version. Use two real stored versions with unequal lengths, first disable or invalidate listing caches, and compare keyword and path-suffix selectors against the storage API. Then repeat with a current-version listing cached and after deleting the current version: a cache of current objects cannot establish that a historical generation is absent. Forwarding the selector alone does not fix this negative-cache boundary; bypass that cache or prove it represents the requested revision. Inspect both _info and its _get_object helper: bypassing only the outer cache still lets the helper incorrectly reject a historical object. A missing explicit generation must not fall through to a latest-version file or directory result. On pinned GCSFS main, info(path, generation=old) selects current metadata while info(path + '#' + old) selects the old object. A native peer-core overlay then reads only b'old' from b'older-version-is-longer' after a three-byte version replaces it. Include nonexistent-generation and directory controls; assert complete contents, not just request arguments or a prefix. Mocking fs.info hides this boundary; reuse the official isolated emulator when real cloud access is unnecessary.
avoid_when: The demonstrated runtime is Python3.12 with official fake-gcs-server1.56.1, not real GCS, full repository CI, every cache mode, concurrent mutation or all versioned backends. The original overlay was not full peer-tree qualification; later selected tests used complete pinned peer production source plus an additional unchanged public regression file. Supplying that source does not test all of it. The metadata defect predates the peer PR. Author aebdcf9 now includes selector forwarding and both cache bypasses; the six-failure result belongs to earlier7dbe183, not that update. All20 unchanged metadata/cache cases pass on aebdcf9, but its concurrent cat_file size lookup still omits the keyword selector: later native whole-file controls reproduce truncation despite the fixed info API. A passing metadata suite does not qualify every caller. Explicit generation and version_aware path parsing are distinct contracts. Preserve unsupported-selector behavior. This owner-led known-case probe is not blinded Scout discovery or measured selector/cost improvement. Coordinate with the existing PR rather than opening a competing implementation.

evidence.note: _info coalesces the explicit generation but calls _get_object(path), whose selector comes only from split_path(path). GCSFile.details passes its separately stored generation to fs.info. Source mechanism, not a real-cloud test.

Public contributor reproduction: two stored versions and the real SDK on the official emulator distinguish keyword metadata from suffix metadata. Pinned peer core over main produces a truncated explicit-generation read. The later metadata-only fork repair is reported separately; neither result claims full peer checkout/CI, real GCS or measured performance.
